blockers.title: G16-4 now forbids blocked-on-ride while the clause it requires and the OBL-6 evidence object both still define it as satisfying, so the contradiction has moved inside a single acceptance class
blockers.subjectEvidence: G16-4 was repaired and now reads, in full: 'Each selected lane emits signedPerLaneClosureEvidence. blocked-on-ride and INACTIVE ride cells are explicit NON-PASS.' Its first sentence discharges the class by requiring emission of signedPerLaneClosureEvidence. That term is defined one node away, byte-identical to v2 and v3, as: 'Required for every selected lane: signed closure bytes/declarations for that lane, OR a named blocked-on-ride standing with owner (DR-120/118/111/106/127 as applicable).' Separately, /independentRelease/evidence/object[2] is also byte-identical to v2 and v3: 'signed per-lane closure emissions for every selected lane, or a named blocked-on-ride standing with owner.'
blockers.governingMeasurement: The v3-to-v4 diff confirms /g16Tests/classes is on the closed roster and was rewritten, while /g16Tests/requiredResults/signedPerLaneClosureEvidence and /independentRelease/evidence are unchanged and were never placed on it. This reviewer raised the same defect at v3 as V3-B2 across three sites; exactly one of the three was repaired, and the successor does not claim otherwise - /appliesFindingsOf/notFoldedThisSuccessor honestly records that the Claude v3 review was in flight. The finding is therefore not a repair failure but a live surviving defect that the v4 repair made structurally tighter.
blockers.counterexample: A component lane and SL-1..SL-4 are all selected. Each emits a named blocked-on-ride standing with an owner and no signed bytes. Against G16-4's first sentence the class is discharged, because signedPerLaneClosureEvidence - by its own definition, which G16-4 incorporates by name - was emitted for every selected lane. Against G16-4's second sentence the same bytes are an explicit NON-PASS. The class now requires the emission of a thing whose definition permits precisely the substitution the class forbids, so G16-4 returns both PASS and NON-PASS on one input and the contract supplies no rule choosing between them. Independently, a release consuming /independentRelease/evidence/object reaches a COMPLETE evidence object on the same bytes, because item 2 is satisfied for every selected lane and nothing in that section withdraws the alternative.
blockers.impact: This is worse than the v3 state, not better. At v3 the override lived in a sibling key and the granting clauses were merely unreconciled; at v4 the prohibition has been written into the acceptance class itself while the definition it invokes still grants, so the contradiction is internal to G16-4 rather than across sections. OBL-6's discharge is the more damaging half: the release evidence object is what a release emits and a coordinator inspects, and it still completes on blocked-on-ride for preview-required lanes. resultSuccessVersusSlotCompleteness asserts cross-section reach ('prevents G16 qualification and independent-release evidence completion'), which makes this a direct contradiction rather than a gap.
blockers.requiredRepair: Amend the two granting clauses rather than adding a third prohibition. In /g16Tests/requiredResults/signedPerLaneClosureEvidence and /independentRelease/evidence/object[2], scope the 'or a named blocked-on-ride standing' alternative to SL-5 and SL-6 explicitly and cross-reference resultSuccessVersusSlotCompleteness. shouldFix.title: The C-CONFLICT-OWNER change class now spans two sub-cases with opposite lawful outcomes, so one corpus cell can satisfy the class while leaving the REFUSE-only rule untested
shouldFix.subjectEvidence: C-CONFLICT-OWNER is defined, unchanged from v2, as 'a changed unit has more than one owner OR an owner outside the universe'. The repaired step 3 and the repaired G16-3 now assign those two halves opposite outcomes: an out-of-universe ownerId is AMBIGUOUS-REFUSE-ONLY, while multiple owners is AMBIGUOUS-CONFLICT and may resolve by SELECT-ENTIRE-UNIVERSE on a complete universe. G16-3 tries to disambiguate with a parenthetical, 'C-CONFLICT-OWNER (multiple owners)', but the change class it names still carries both halves, and /g16Tests/corpus was not on the roster.
shouldFix.counterexample: The corpus coverage law requires a result per changeClass cell. A harness builds its single C-CONFLICT-OWNER cell using two owners and resolves it by SELECT-ENTIRE-UNIVERSE. Every coverage obligation is met and G16-3 passes. The out-of-universe ownerId case - one of the four REFUSE-only conditions the v4 repair was written to install - is never exercised in any cell, because no change class isolates it. The repair is stated in the law and in the class prose but is not forced by the corpus, which is what the live DR-G16 row buys when it requires 'forced dependency/ownership mutations'.
shouldFix.impact: A negative-test corpus whose change class does not determine the expected outcome cannot enforce the distinction the class was repaired to draw. This is the residue of repairing the law and the class while leaving the corpus that feeds them off the roster.
shouldFix.suggestedFix: Split C-CONFLICT-OWNER into C-MULTI-OWNER ('more than one owner', CONFLICT) and C-OUT-OF-UNIVERSE-OWNER ('an ownerId outside the comparison-basis universe', REFUSE-only), and drop G16-3's parenthetical once the class names are unambiguous. systemicObservation: v4 is the strongest successor in this chain and the first whose repairs are all real at the clause that states them. The pattern this reviewer flagged at v3 has partly corrected: v4 rewrote G16-3 and G16-4 in place rather than adding another override layer. But the roster is still drawn around the clauses a reviewer named rather than around the clauses that state the superseded rule, and every finding above except V4-S1 is a direct consequence. The mechanical test is available and cheap: for each honestyRepairs entry, grep the artifact for the terms the repair abolishes - 'trigger', 'or a named blocked-on-ride standing' - and put every hit on the roster before authoring. Run against v4 that test yields exactly V4-B1 and V4-S2, which are two of this verdict's five substantive findings. A v5 that adopts it would converge; a v5 that keeps sizing the roster to the previous review's finding list will keep shedding one or two survivors per cycle.
verdictBasis: One blocker and four SHOULD-FIX findings survive. The dispatch admits ACCEPT only at zero blockers and zero SHOULD-FIX. All six claimed repairs are real - trigger table out of the selector output, G16-3 REFUSE-only, previousCommittedTree named, joint fixpoint, advisories booked, IR NON-PASS - and this reviewer confirms each against the subject's bytes. Three findings this reviewer raised at v3 are discharged. What blocks acceptance is the one v3 blocker that was repaired at a single site out of three, whose two surviving sites now contradict the repaired class directly rather than merely sitting beside it.
verdictStatement: v4 repairs everything it claims to repair. The trigger table is gone from the selector output and ID-DEP-C6, G16-3 is REFUSE-only for missing, out-of-universe, undeclared and incomplete-universe cases, previousCommittedTree is named with a non-git fallback and an execution-time digest pin, the two expansions run to a joint fixpoint, the Claude v2 advisories are booked, and a failed or INACTIVE IR cell is an explicit NON-PASS. It also discloses honestly that the Claude v3 review was in flight and that its findings require a v5. That disclosure is why the surviving blocker is not a repair failure - but it is still a live defect, and it is now sharper than it was: G16-4 was rewritten to make blocked-on-ride an explicit NON-PASS while the clause G16-4 requires by name, signedPerLaneClosureEvidence, still defines that emission as satisfiable by blocked-on-ride, and the OBL-6 release evidence object still completes on it independently. One acceptance class now returns both PASS and NON-PASS on the same bytes. Four SHOULD-FIX findings stand alongside it: a re-measurement block added outside the closed roster, a honesty entry claiming a fourth path was cleaned when it was not, a conflict change class that no longer determines its expected outcome, and a live-pin pointer two generations stale. DR-121 remains OPEN; DR-G16 remains PROPOSED, not QUALIFIED.
authorityOfThisVerdict: This verdict is a reviewer opinion recorded for coordinator disposition. It applies nothing, edits no subject, marks no row SATISFIED, marks no gate QUALIFIED, authorizes no implementation, mints no D-096 (A), and does not touch docs/v2/architecture/08-decision-and-readiness-register.md or docs/coop/COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md.
coordinatorNote: The v5 roster needs five paths beyond whatever the concurrent v4 reviewer names: /g16Tests/requiredResults/signedPerLaneClosureEvidence and /independentRelease/evidence/object/2 for the blocker, /g16Tests/requiredResults/skippedLaneProof and /g16Tests/corpus/changeClasses for V4-S2 and V4-S3, and /recordedInputs for V4-S4. Add /reMeasurementAtV5 to the roster text itself, or restore v2's succession-metadata clause. None of this is design work - every design decision in v4 is sound and independently verified above; what remains is propagating four of them into clauses that still state the superseded rule. Two process notes: the Claude v3 findings were correctly deferred to v5 rather than silently absorbed, and that deferral should be closed out explicitly in v5's appliesFindingsOf, since three of the six are already discharged by v4's Codex-driven repairs and only V3-B2, V3-S2 and the V3-A advisories remain live. Separately, this verdict certifies nothing about v4's characterization of the Codex v3 findings, which was not readable under this dispatch.
